detector_rule.instructions: Choose the safest bounded correction for wrong detector attribution in the scalar ray model before any Blender test.
criteria: Add failing CPU regressions, then require detectors to lie ahead of BS2 and route each output ray to its nearest positive sphere entry among both detectors; if the target is not first, a tie occurs, or a detector encloses the BS2 origin, mark power unresolved with explicit status and preserve the ledger. Reverify no regression.
Keep checking only whether each target sphere is hit at any distance, even when another detector is encountered first.
Implement a full general-purpose occlusion renderer/GPU ray tracer immediately.

width_gate.instructions: Decide whether to change the hard 0.02 BU centroid gate now that an explicit positive beam waist exists, while avoiding a false physical overlap claim.
criteria: For positive beam waist use a documented threshold based on transverse offset (for example O>=0.01, equivalently s<=w*sqrt(-2 ln 0.01)), while retaining direction, aperture, first-detector gates; keep the 0.02 BU centroid gate only for legacy beam_waist=None. Test the wide-beam counterexample and rejected tiny-overlap case, keep Blender gate closed.
Keep the 0.02 BU gate even for finite beam waist, but explicitly document that high-overlap wider beams are unresolved by design and do not call it a coherent beam model beyond that gate.
Drop all centroid, direction and detector checks whenever beam_waist is present.
